title: Request bodies and Pydantic models

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE
POST/PUT requests often carry new or changed data in a JSON body. A Pydantic model states field types and constraints in one place; FastAPI parses and validates the model before calling the endpoint.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
A sign-up form sends an email and age; the model makes those fields an explicit contract.
If this part is omitted: Without a body model, the input shape is undocumented and relies on repeated manual checks.

Request: POST /users  body={"email":"ada@example.com","age":20}
Response: 200 OK; JSON: {"email":"ada@example.com","age":20}

spans.text:
LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`from pydantic import BaseModel, Field` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`class UserInput(BaseModel):` — Defines a Pydantic data model; its field types form the request-body contract.
`email: str` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`age: int = Field(ge=13, le=120)` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`@app.post("/users")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def create_user(user: UserInput):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"email": user.email, "age": user.age}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
PRACTICE: CHECK IT WITH AN HTTP CLIENT
This complete file calls the app locally with TestClient; it does not open a server port. Install `httpx` for TestClient.
COMPLETE RUNNABLE CLIENT TEST
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()

class UserInput(BaseModel):
    email: str
    age: int = Field(ge=13, le=120)

@app.post("/users")
async def create_user(user: UserInput):
    return {"email": user.email, "age": user.age}

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.post("/users", json={"email": "ada@example.com", "age": 20})
    print(response.status_code, response.json())

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`from pydantic import BaseModel, Field` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`class UserInput(BaseModel):` — Defines a Pydantic data model; its field types form the request-body contract.
`email: str` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`age: int = Field(ge=13, le=120)` — Declares an expected model field and type; omitting it changes the body contract.
`@app.post("/users")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def create_user(user: UserInput):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"email": user.email, "age": user.age}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
`from fastapi.testclient import TestClient` — Imports TestClient so an HTTP request can exercise the app without opening a server port.
`with TestClient(app) as client:` — Creates a test HTTP client for the app and closes it when the context ends.
`response = client.post("/users", json={"email": "ada@example.com", "age": 20})` — Runs work for this request; its result or side effect affects the response.
`print(response.status_code, response.json())` — Reads and prints both the HTTP status code and parsed JSON response.
COMMON MISTAKES
Treating all JSON as an unchecked `dict`; distinguish required and optional fields in the model.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Submit the expected body in `/docs`, then remove a field and observe the automatic 422 response.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: In Pydantic v2, `str | None` permits null; `= None` also makes the field optional. Type and requiredness are separate decisions.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Never trust client values. Model validation does not replace business rules, authorization, or protection of private data.
